title: Biochemical-constrained generative AI yields experimentally active antimicrobial peptides against E. coli
summary: A University of Hong Kong-led team used a conditional variational autoencoder constrained by biochemical properties and a random-forest activity classifier to generate and prioritize antimicrobial peptides. In vitro testing of 54 generated peptides found 18.5% with MIC ≤10 μg/mL and 38.9% with MIC ≤50 μg/mL against the study’s E. coli model; nine peptides were classified as both active and non-toxic in the reported assays.
ai_technology: CVAE-BIO: conditional variational autoencoder with biochemical constraints and a random-forest antimicrobial-activity classifier
organization: The University of Hong Kong; University of Hong Kong-Shenzhen Hospital; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: In vitro testing of 54 generated peptides found 18.5% with MIC ≤10 μg/mL and 38.9% with MIC ≤50 μg/mL against the study’s E. coli model; nine peptides were classified as both active and non-toxic in the reported assays.
evidence.unknown: Validation is in vitro, primarily against E. coli ATCC 25922; it is not evidence of treatment efficacy in animals or humans. The reported nine active/non-toxic peptides are assay-defined candidate hits, not validated drugs. This paper generated a different peptide set and used different training/design and testing workflows from the earlier C. acnes deep-learning, bullfrog-genome AMPlify, and LSTM Klebsiella sepsis studies in this ledger; do not treat the general AMP topic as a duplicate.
evidence.ai_role: The CVAE generated peptide sequences subject to predefined biochemical constraints; the random forest ranked activity using 30 biochemical descriptors. Researchers synthesized/tested 54 generated peptides in vitro, measured MIC and hemolysis, and reported the active/non-toxic subset.
